question_text: How must you safeguard your motorcycle against unauthorized use?

options.text: By removing the ignition key
By locking the steering
By engaging top gear

correct_answers.text: By removing the ignition key
By locking the steering

comment: To avoid other people to use your motorcycle, remove the ignition key and lock the steering.

question_text: You want to park your motorcycle on its prop stand. What do you have to consider?

options.text: The surface under the prop stand must be firm
You must extend the prop stand to the end position
You should only park your motorcycle on an upward slope

correct_answers.text: The surface under the prop stand must be firm
You must extend the prop stand to the end position

comment: To avoid your motorcycle to tip over, make sure the surface is firm and can support the weight of the motorcycle and that you swing the side stand all the way up to the stop.

question_text: You want to park your motorcycle on its main stand. What do you have to consider?

options.text: The surface under the main stand must be firm
You may only use the main stand to park your motorcycle for a short time

correct_answers.text: The surface under the main stand must be firm

comment: To avoid your motorcycle to tip over, make sure the surface is firm and can support the weight of the motorcycle. You can park your bike that way for a short or long time.

question_text: Where should you not park a motorcycle (using main or side stand)?

options.text: On soft ground
Where the parking surface is a steep downward slope
On firm ground

correct_answers.text: On soft ground
Where the parking surface is a steep downward slope

comment: To avoid your motorcycle to tip over, make sure the surface is firm and can support the weight of the motorcycle. Also make sure that the surface is not too steep downwards which would make the main or side stand unsafe and at risk of tipping over

question_text: Which precautionary measures must you take when parking a motorcycle?

options.text: Park on firm ground
Remove the ignition key
Lock the handlebar

correct_answers.text: Park on firm ground
Remove the ignition key
Lock the handlebar

comment: You must make sure that no other people can use your motorcycle by removing the ignition key and locking in the handlebar/steering. Also make sure that the groud is firm to avoid the motorcycle to tip over.

question_text: You want to park your motorcycle. What must you consider?

options.text: The parking surface must be firm
You can lean the motorcycle against a lamppost if you put it into gear
You must switch on the dipped headlight

correct_answers.text: The parking surface must be firm

comment: When parking, to avoid your motorcycle to tip over, make sure the surface is firm and can support the weight of the motorcycle.

question_text: How do you secure your motorcycle against being used without permission?

options.text: - remove the ignition key
- close the steering lock
- disconnect the battery

correct_answers.text: - remove the ignition key
- close the steering lock

comment: The steering lock prevents steering in the event of unauthorised access. The engine cannot be started by removing the ignition key.

question_text: What must you be aware of when using a prop stand?

options.text: The gradient of the parking place
The characteristics of the ground surface
That the prop stand is completely folded away before driving off

correct_answers.text: The gradient of the parking place
The characteristics of the ground surface
That the prop stand is completely folded away before driving off

comment: If the side stand is not fully retracted, it can cause a fall when cornering. If the slope is too great, the motorbike can slide forward because the side stand folds in on its own. If the ground is too soft, the motorbike may sink until it falls.

question_text: What should be noted when using the prop stand?

options.text: Where possible, the motorbike should not be parked on a slope
The prop stand should be fully extended
The prop stand switch can prevent you driving off with the prop stand extended

correct_answers.text: Where possible, the motorbike should not be parked on a slope
The prop stand should be fully extended
The prop stand switch can prevent you driving off with the prop stand extended

comment:
If the side stand is still folded out and you engage a gear, the side stand switch will automatically switch off the engine. The side stand switch is a safety measure that prevents you from riding off with the side stand folded out.
The side stand is designed for parking a motorbike. Try to avoid slopes when parking. Always make sure that your motorbike is stable and that the side stand is fully extended to avoid danger and damage.

question_text: How must you safeguard your vehicle against theft?

options.text: By removing the ignition key, engaging the steering wheel lock and closing the windows
By locking the doors and boot
By activating the differential lock

correct_answers.text: By removing the ignition key, engaging the steering wheel lock and closing the windows
By locking the doors and boot

comment: To secure the car against theft, you must first close all the windows and doors. The ignition key must be removed in any case. Snap the steering wheel lock into place to additionally secure the car.

question_text: What must you do when leaving your car?

options.text: Before opening the door, look out for traffic behind
Secure the vehicle against rolling away
Secure the vehicle against unauthorized use

correct_answers.text: Before opening the door, look out for traffic behind
Secure the vehicle against rolling away
Secure the vehicle against unauthorized use

comment: Before leaving the vehicle, you have to protect it against rolling away uncontrolled, for example on a downhill slope. Before exiting you have to make sure not to endanger other road users. This also applies to your passengers. Opening doors carelessly when getting out is a common cause of accidents. The vehicle must also be protected against unauthorized use.

question_text: Your car is standing on the edge of the roadway. What should you do when getting into the car?

options.text: Let passengers get into the car, if possible, from the pavement
Open the doors on the roadway side only when traffic permits
The doors on the right-hand side can always be opened without danger

correct_answers.text: Let passengers get into the car, if possible, from the pavement
Open the doors on the roadway side only when traffic permits

comment: When entering and exiting, you must take care not to endanger the other road users. The entry from the right - from the sidewalk - is safer, but not without any danger. Before you open the doors, make sure that the traffic situation permits that. Make sure that there are no pedestrians or cyclists on the sidewalk at this time.

question_text: What is important when children are getting in and out of a car?

options.text: Let the children in or out, if possible, on the pavement side
Let the children in or out on the roadway side only under supervision
Children are not allowed to get in or out of a car on public roads

correct_answers.text: Let the children in or out, if possible, on the pavement side
Let the children in or out on the roadway side only under supervision

comment: As a car driver, you should make sure that children get on and off directly on the sidewalk. If the situation does not allow this, they should only get in or out on the side of the road under the supervision of an adult. Children are seen worse and are unpredictable in their behavior.

question_text: What should you call the attention of your passengers to before exiting?

options.text: - they should heed the traffic flowing on the left-side
- they should heed the pedestrians walking on the right-side
- cyclists are required to wait on cycle paths

correct_answers.text: - they should heed the traffic flowing on the left-side
- they should heed the pedestrians walking on the right-side

comment: As a car driver you must take the necessary measures to avoid accidents or traffic disruptions when passengers leave the vehicle. Point that out to passengers when they get off on a bike path. Cyclists are not required to wait on bike paths. Anyone entering or leaving the car may not endanger other road users.

question_text: Why may you not exit now?

options.text: Because [of the cyclist]
Because of the motorbike
Because [of the pedestrian]

correct_answers.text: Because [of the cyclist]

comment: Anyone getting in or out of the car must behave in such a way as to avoid endangering other road users. An approaching cyclist can be seen in your left-hand side mirror, you must let him pass first.

question_text: You have stopped in a parking strip and now want to exit your vehicle. What must you do in this situation?

options.text: - by looking in my left-hand exterior rear-view mirror before opening the door
- by glancing over my left shoulder before opening the door
- just by looking through the slightly opened door

correct_answers.text: - by looking in my left-hand exterior rear-view mirror before opening the door
- by glancing over my left shoulder before opening the door

comment: Before you open the door and leave the vehicle, check in the left-hand mirror that no one is coming from behind. You must also look to your left to make sure that there are no other vehicles in your blind spot.

question_text: When leaving your car, how do you secure it against unauthorised use?

options.text: I lock the doors
I close the windows
I activate the child-safety lock

correct_answers.text: I lock the doors
I close the windows

comment: You have to make sure that no unauthorised persons use your car. Therefore, remove the key from the starter and make sure that all windows and doors are closed.

question_text: You want to let a child out of your car. What should you be aware of when doing so?

options.text: - exit the car on the same side as the footpath
- not have to cross over the carriageway
- be warned of possible dangers when getting out of the car

correct_answers.text: - exit the car on the same side as the footpath
- not have to cross over the carriageway
- be warned of possible dangers when getting out of the car

comment: As a car driver, you should make sure that children get on and off directly on the pavement side. If the situation does not allow this, they should only get in or out of the vehicle on the carriageway side under supervision and with prior warning of possible dangers. Children are harder to see and their behaviour is unpredictable, so you should make sure that they no longer have to cross the road.
